answer:
Hypothesis (data-grounded answer to "In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapse and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increase simultaneously?"):

**The 17th century BCE (1700 a.C. / siglo XVII a.C.)** — in the 100-year bin whose start is 1700 BCE, Pottery Form diversity collapses from Z = +0.74 to Z = −1.13 (ΔZ = −1.87, the largest negative form-slope in the entire series) while Pottery Decoration diversity simultaneously jumps from Z = −0.48 to Z = +0.97 (ΔZ = +1.45, the largest positive decoration-slope in the entire series, alongside the 4100 BCE rise). This is the only century in the whole 4300–500 BCE record where both a form-collapse and a decoration-increase coincide in the same bin; the pattern persists at the flat collapsed level (form −1.13, decoration +0.97) for the following ~10 centuries. The transition is robust: it is also detected in the confirmation analysis on the annual interpolated series with a 100-year rolling mean (smoothed Δform = −0.87 ≤ threshold; smoothed Δdeco = +0.79 ≥ threshold). Archaeologically this coincides with the end of the Nordic Middle Bronze Age / onset of the Late Bronze Age transition in northern Germany (Woserin/Mecklenburg region, Feeser et al. 2019 context), consistent with a socio-economic restructuring in which standardized decoration gained diversity while vessel-form diversity collapsed.

payload.hypothesis: In the 17th century BCE (bin starting 1700 BCE; 1700–1601 BCE), the diversity of pottery form collapsed (Z: +0.74 → −1.13, ΔZ = −1.87, the largest negative form-slope in the 4300–500 BCE record) while the diversity of pottery decoration simultaneously increased (Z: −0.48 → +0.97, ΔZ = +1.45, a top-percentile positive decoration-slope), and this anti-phase transition is the only century in the entire record where both conditions coincide in the same 100-year bin under empirically fixed 5%/95% slope thresholds; the new regime then persisted for ~10 centuries (form flat at −1.13, decoration at +0.97/+1.53).

thresholds.collapse_form: dZ_form <= -0.492 (5th percentile of empirical form-slope distribution, n=38)
thresholds.increase_decoration: dZ_deco >= +0.693 (95th percentile of empirical decoration-slope distribution, n=38)
thresholds.simultaneity: same 100-yr bin (primary); ±100 yr window (sensitivity, same unique result)

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded capital.csv (decimal=','), mapped BCE→CE=-BCE and verified numeric identity with time_series_data.csv raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration on all 37 overlapping century bins (max diff 0.0). 2) Computed century-to-century slopes dZ (newer minus older) on the raw 100-yr values (primary). 3) Fixed collapse/increase thresholds as the 5th/95th percentiles of the empirical slope distributions before inspecting any result. 4) Detected bins satisfying both conditions in the same century (unique: 1700 BCE) plus ±100-yr sensitivity and 100-yr-rolling-mean confirmation on the annual _inter series (both criteria also met; Spearman corr of slopes ~0.57–0.58). 5) Exported full evidence table (slope_evidence_table.csv) and the executed script (analysis_pottery.py).
